extra.message: User-controlled 'host' parameter from request.GET['host'] is concatenated directly into an os.system() shell command string via 'ping -c 1 ' + host. An attacker with the internal ops token (or if the token env var is unset) can execute arbitrary OS commands.

User-controlled 'fragment' from request.GET['fragment'] is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string: Template('Result: ' + fragment).render(). This enables Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) leading to arbitrary Python code execution.

User-supplied data from request.body or request.GET is deserialized using pickle.loads(). The pickle module is fundamentally unsafe when loading untrusted data and allows arbitrary code execution. Data source at line 65-69 accepts raw request body or GET parameter 'blob' with optional base64 wrapping.

XML parser from lxml is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False, explicitly enabling external entity resolution. XML data is parsed directly from request.body at line 163. This allows XXE attacks for file disclosure, SSRF, and denial of service.

User-controlled 'lane' parameter from request.GET or request.POST is passed directly to django.shortcuts.redirect() without any URL validation. An attacker can craft a URL that redirects users to an arbitrary external domain for phishing.

The Origin request header is reflected back verbatim in Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This mirrors any requesting origin with credentials allowed, enabling cross-origin attacks with session cookie access.

The raw request body and the Authorization header are logged via logger.warning(). This can expose bearer tokens, API keys, and other sensitive authentication credentials to log files which may have weaker access controls.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The course_roster_fold_036 endpoint has no authentication check (unlike most other /ops/ endpoints which call _wrk_gate). It is publicly accessible and returns internal operational metadata.
The course_identity_ping_338 endpoint has no authentication check, making it publicly accessible to any unauthenticated user. Unlike most other /ops/ endpoints, _wrk_gate is not called.
The response explicitly disables X-XSS-Protection by setting it to '0' and sets Content-Security-Policy to an empty string, removing all CSP protections for this endpoint.

The 'length' parameter from request.GET is converted to int() without any upper bound validation and used to control a loop that generates random characters. A large value causes excessive CPU and memory consumption.
The course_trace_panel_537 endpoint exposes internal environment variables (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE) and filesystem paths (BASE_EXPORT_DIR) in the JSON response, revealing internal deployment details.

A hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY 'unsafe-local-dev-key-change-me' is used when the DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. If deployed without setting this env var, cryptographic protections (sessions, CSRF tokens, password reset tokens) use a known secret.

All demo user accounts created by the seed command use a hardcoded password 'DemoPass123!'. While this is a seed script, if run in a non-ephemeral environment, these accounts would be accessible with known credentials.

Authentication verifier secrets are hardcoded in the source code: known dict with handle-to-verifier mappings ('north'/'4812', 'south'/'5930'). These credential-like values should be stored outside the codebase.

SSL certificate verification is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context(). The HTTP request to the partner endpoint will not validate the server certificate, opening the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks.
